transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Time: 15:00 EDT
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Owen Martinez (Redwood SE), Janelle Park (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Argentum CTO), Daniel Roe (Argentum Lead ML Eng), Lucia Gomez (Argentum Prod Ops), Aaron Blake (Argentum SRE)

Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and prefix/K V cache recommendations for Argentum's user-session assistant product. Covered cost model scenarios (hosted vs dedicated), prefetch approach for 3 session types, capacity planning, security questions (VPC, KMS, SOC2), and concrete next steps: run benchmark with their prompt set, send cost sheet, grant sandbox access.

Topics Covered:
- Prefetch patterns (session-based, conversational sessionization)
- KV/prefix cache sizing and eviction TTLs
- Batch size vs latency tradeoffs and concurrency envelope
- Hosted vs Dedicated cost scenarios and fallback policies
- Security: VPC, KMS/H S M, audit logs, RBAC

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): All right, thanks everyone for joining, uh, we'll run for about 45 minutes, go through the Optimize console playbook for prefetch and capacity planning, and leave some time for your questions. Sound good?
[00:14] Priya (Argentum): Yep, sounds good. Thanks Maya. Quick note, we're on EDT here, and Daniel's joining from London but he hates early mornings, so appreciate the timing.
[00:28] Owen (Redwood): Quick intros — I'm Owen, I'll be your SE, I'll run the benchmark work with your prompts, and Janelle will show a couple of console screens.
[00:42] Daniel (Argentum): Great. Our main goal today is to see how Redwood Optimize recommendations can reduce per-token costs while meeting our 800ms p95 latency SLO for the customer-facing assistant. We have three session types: short intent queries (~15 tokens), medium follow-ups (~60 tokens), and long summarizations (~1.2k tokens).
[01:05] Janelle (Redwood): Ok perfect, that's helpful. Before we dive in, can you tell us current stack and where inference runs today?
[01:12] Daniel (Argentum): We're mostly on-prem for sensitive workloads, self-hosted model cluster using mixed A100 and 80G boxes, some requests still hit a cloud endpoint (for non-PII flows). We imagine moving more traffic to Redwood Dedicated or Private depending on SLA.
[01:30] Lucia (Argentum): Also curious about session cache TTLs — we currently have a memory store that keeps last 10 turns per user, but we don't prefetch KV caches on session start.
[01:40] Owen (Redwood): That is a common pattern. Prefetching the prefix/K V for the initial system prompt and recent turns can dramatically reduce token generation on the model side because you already have warmed KV and can avoid re-sending the full prompt.
[01:55] Maya (Redwood): We'll show three recommended profiles: conservative prefetch (warm only system + last turn), balanced (system + last 3 turns + recent embeddings), and aggressive (entire last 10 turns + lookahead for expected queries). We'll map each to cost/delay numbers.
[02:12] Priya (Argentum): How do you quantify costs — is it tokens, GPU time, or concurrency? Our CFO wants dollars per 1M sessions.
[02:23] Owen (Redwood): Good q. Optimize's model is token + model-time. For hosted we price per-token plus a small compute premium; Dedicated turns into throughput-based pricing with reserved GPUs. The cost model workbook we'll send maps session mix -> tokens saved -> GPU hours -> $ per M sessions.
[02:41] Daniel (Argentum): Do you account for batching improvements if we increase client concurrency? Our client side is fine, we can batch at the gateway to hit larger batch sizes.
[02:52] Janelle (Redwood): Yes — one of the slides shows how throughput scales: small batches (1-4) favor latency but high cost per token, mid batches (8-16) reduce per-token cost with small latency impact, large batches (32+) are best for cost but hurt tail latency. If you control gateway concurrency you can shape the batch distribution to hit an economical sweet spot.
[03:17] Aaron (Argentum): Our p95 target of 800ms is tight for long summarization; how do you handle long seqs re: batching?
[03:26] Owen (Redwood): For long tokens we recommend sessionization + async worker for background summarization or streaming partial replies. For the p95, we advise smaller dedicated pools that prioritize low-latency queues. That's where Dedicated helps because you can reserve a low-latency pool for summarizations.
[03:44] Priya (Argentum): And fallback policies? If the Dedicated pool is saturated, can Redwood route to hosted cheaper model?
[03:51] Maya (Redwood): Yes, smart routing allows fallbacks. You can route by latency, cost, or compliance — for sensitive traffic you'd avoid hosted fallback, but for non-PII you can define a cheaper fallback model. The console can show per-route policies.
[04:05] Daniel (Argentum): Let's talk TTLs — Lucia, what's your typical retention?
[04:09] Lucia (Argentum): We keep last 10 turns in memory for 30 minutes. After that we drop to cold storage.
[04:16] Janelle (Redwood): For prefix/K V caches, our recommendation is TTLs aligned to active session lifetime. Example: for short sessions TTL 60s, medium 300s, long sessions 30 min. Eviction based on active memory plus an LRU policy reduces unnecessary prefetch cost.
[04:34] Priya (Argentum): Does the prefetch itself cost tokens? I mean if we prefetch 10 turns that's extra calls, right?
[04:41] Owen (Redwood): Prefetch is cheaper than on-demand generation because you typically issue a warm batch call that caches KV — it's a small one-time cost but it saves on generation tokens if users continue the conversation. The workbook models net savings: prefetch overhead vs expected generation avoidance.
[04:58] Daniel (Argentum): Show us a scenario — for our session mix, what's the net savings for balanced prefetch?
[05:04] Janelle (Redwood): (screen share noises) So here's a quick sim: with your mix 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long — balanced prefetch reduces token generation by ~22% and GPU time by ~18% at the 95th percentile of sessions, assuming a 20% cache hit rate on session continuation. That maps to about $0.32 less per 1k sessions on hosted assumptions.
[05:28] Priya (Argentum): Hmm, that's interesting. What's the sensitivity if cache hit rate drops to 10%?
[05:33] Owen (Redwood): Then the net savings drop to single digits; prefetch TTLs and accurate sessionization are important. If you can't get >15% continuation, conservative prefetch is safer.
[05:45] Aaron (Argentum): Security check — if we warm caches in Redwood Hosted, will any prompt text be persisted? We need to confirm PII rules.
[05:54] Maya (Redwood): Hosted can be configured with minimal retention and redaction rules; for strict PII/regulated data Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) keeps everything in your control and K M S integrations with H S M for keys. We'll share the SOC2 + VPC docs.
[06:10] Priya (Argentum): Ok send those. Also, how do we revoke caches if we detect unwanted data mid-session?
[06:17] Janelle (Redwood): You can invalidate a session cache via API call immediately; we recommend detection triggers on the application side to call an invalidate endpoint.
[06:27] Daniel (Argentum): About the benchmark — what do you need from us?
[06:31] Owen (Redwood): Your 5k prompt set, representative concurrency profile, and target latency SLOs. We'll run against a mirrored model configuration; if you require exact model we can run a self-hosted run or use Dedicated with pinned model.
[06:45] Lucia (Argentum): Will you simulate client batching behavior or should we provide gateway logs?
[06:50] Owen (Redwood): Gateway logs are ideal, but we can run a few synthetic concurrency shapes: steady (10 qps), spiky (bursts to 200 qps), and low (1-2 qps) to show sensitivity.
[07:02] Priya (Argentum): Let's pivot to console — Janelle demo the Optimize rule-set for prefetch.
[07:08] Janelle (Redwood): (screen clicking) In the console you define a profile per route — here is the prefetch policy editor. You can set lookahead depth, TTL, cost threshold, and fallback model. Notice the expected token delta preview on the right — that's Optimize's sim.
[07:27] Daniel (Argentum): Is there a way to run A/B test of prefetch aggressiveness?
[07:31] Janelle (Redwood): Yes, canary and A/B are built-in. You can allocate 10% of traffic to aggressive prefetch and measure token delta + latencies. The console stores event stats per-campaign.
[07:43] Priya (Argentum): How about autoscale coupling? If you prefetch aggressively do you risk sudden GPU spikes?
[07:50] Owen (Redwood): Aggressive prefetch can cause short-lived spikes; we recommend burst capacity or rate-limited prefetching during peak windows. The console supports burst buckets and autoscale policies tuned for prefetch load.
[08:06] Daniel (Argentum): Let's talk numbers — show dedicated vs hosted cost for a million sessions.
[08:11] Janelle (Redwood): (pointing) On hosted assumptions with your mix, baseline cost is X per 1M sessions, balanced prefetch reduces to X-320, dedicated at 50% utilization gives Y which is lower per session but requires commit. We put full numbers in the sheet — we'll send it.
[08:32] Priya (Argentum): CFO will ask about run-rate commitments — what's the smallest Dedicated footprint?
[08:38] Maya (Redwood): You can start with a small reserved pool (2-4 A100-equivalent GPUs) and use burst to absorb peaks. We also offer hybrid where you keep sensitive traffic in Private and route non-sensitive to Hosted.
[08:55] Aaron (Argentum): On RBAC and audit logs — we need admin separation, read-only for ops, and ability to pull audit trails for last 90 days.
[09:03] Maya (Redwood): RBAC, SSO via SAML, audit logs with export, and retention tiers are supported; the SOC2 doc details retention. We'll attach that link.
[09:12] Daniel (Argentum): Any gotchas on model compilers/quantization affecting KV caches? We've seen degraded quality when quantizing some Llama forks.
[09:20] Owen (Redwood): Quantization can affect generation quality; our Optimize recommendations include suggested quantization profile per model and a validation eval set. For KV caches, the runtime manages compatibility; if you roll a quantized variant we test retrieval consistency.
[09:36] Lucia (Argentum): If we want to keep latency tight for short intents, could we pre-compute embeddings and store in cache?
[09:42] Janelle (Redwood): Yes embeddings precomputation is a common optimization; storing recent user embeddings and doing similarity lookup avoids long prefix sends. That sits alongside KV caching.
[09:55] Priya (Argentum): Ok, final section — timeline and acceptance criteria for pilot.
[09:59] Maya (Redwood): Pilot recommended scope: 2-week sandbox, run Schneider-style bench with your 5k prompts, measure p95, token reduction, and cost delta. Acceptance: <800ms p95 for the priority route and >15% net token savings for the assistant traffic.
[10:16] Daniel (Argentum): That seems fair. Priya, any legal/process blockers?
[10:20] Priya (Argentum): We'll need standard DPA review and non-production access to sandbox environment. Also want to confirm encryption-at-rest using our K M S.
[10:29] Maya (Redwood): We'll share DPA and K M S integration notes — most customers use CloudK M S or Vault H S M.
[10:35] (cross talk)
[10:40] Aaron (Argentum): One practical question: how do we monitor cache hit rates?
[10:44] Owen (Redwood): Console exposes cache hit/miss metrics per-route, TTL histograms, and memory usage. We also emit traces you can pipe to your observability stack.
[10:55] Daniel (Argentum): Let's close with open risks — Priya, anything else?
[10:59] Priya (Argentum): Only that our security review takes about 2-3 weeks; can Redwood coordinate a SOC2/infra deep dive with our security folks?
[11:07] Maya (Redwood): Yes, we can schedule a security deep dive — SE and Security team will join.
[11:12] Janelle (Redwood): I'll drop links to the console docs and a short video on prefetch best practices.
[11:18] Maya (Redwood): Great. Quick recap: Owen runs benchmark, Maya sends cost workbook & SOC2/VPC docs, Janelle shares console links & video, Argentum provides prompt set and concurrency profile. We'll aim to have sandbox ready by 2026-05-11.
[11:33] Priya (Argentum): Thanks all. Looking forward to the benchmark.
[11:36] Maya (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the attachments.
[11:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: Some product names auto-transcribed (e.g., "K V cache" as separate letters) — original discussion referenced Redwood Optimize console and prefix/KV cache prefetching.
